chunks: Shu'ayb narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If you take land by the willing consent of its owners upon a condition that you stipulated with them, then all surplus in its cultivation belongs to you, provided that you fulfill your agreement with them. And if you repair something in it or introduce a building in it, then you are entitled to the rent of its buildings, except what is in the hands of its dahāqīn.

key_terms.تَقَبَّلْتَ: you took or accepted land under an agreement
key_terms.شَرْطٍ: a stipulated condition in the agreement

ai.seo_question: When a person leases or takes land on agreed terms, who owns the surplus produce and the benefit of improvements made to it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about taking land on agreed terms with the consent of its owners. It establishes that the cultivator is entitled to the surplus produce and to the benefit of repairs or buildings he adds, so long as he fulfills the agreed conditions, with an exception for what remains under the possession of the dahāqīn.
